correctness.rationale: The proof is complete. Nonzero translation rows are indexed by the difference set \(A-B\). If the two unoriented support differences differ, all four differences are distinct, every row is a point mass, and the support is \(4p\). If they align, there are exactly three rows: two singleton rows contribute \(p\) each, and the middle row is a two-point Fourier transform. Because multiplication by the nonzero support difference permutes all \(p\)-th roots, that row has exactly one zero iff the stated cross-ratio is a \(p\)-th root of unity, and otherwise none, giving \(3p-1\) or \(3p\). The explicit examples attain all three values. Finite verifier cases are consistency checks only.
